headline: Red Sox head west looking for answers after suspension nightmare
morning_brew: It's been a rough week at Fenway, and now we're packing our bags for the West Coast while missing key pieces. Nate Eaton picking up a three-game suspension after that bench-clearing brawl on Tuesday is just the cherry on top of a messy stretch. You hate to see the league step in like that, but when things get out of hand the way they did against the Nationals, someone is gonna pay the price. My neighbor Rick already has a theory about how the league office treats Boston differently than the rest of the clubs, and honestly, I'm finding it harder to talk him down these days.

The team is sitting at 37-48, and frankly, we need a serious reset before the Angels series gets underway tonight. We've got to find a way to manufacture runs without the guys who are sidelined, and the starting rotation really needs to step up and give us some length. It's tough to watch the bullpen get taxed night after night, but that's what happens when you're constantly playing from behind. I'm just hoping the change of scenery is exactly what this clubhouse needs to get the wheels turning again.

Elsewhere, the C's are still making headlines with the Jaylen Brown trade to the 76ers, leaving us all wondering what the roster will look like next season. It's a huge shift in direction, and with the Bruins also navigating the early stages of their offseason, all eyes are on the front office to see how they rebuild. For now, all we can do is hope the Sox can find a pulse out in Anaheim. Let's hope they show up ready to play because we cannot afford to dig an even deeper hole.

news_digest.dans_take: Hard to see a guy like that leave, but that's the reality of the business.
